newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--As a first step to bringing calm and stability to Tirana, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou pledged a 20 billion drachma loan to the neighbouring country, as soon as the situation in the country was stabilised.

--Misinformation about the demand for shares and insider trading were the main volations of stock exchange legislation by protagonists in last year's Delta scandal, the Capital Market Commission says.
--The Bank of Greece will introduce new guidelines on the operation of foreign exchange, following legislation submitted yesterday.

--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, has revised its forecasted 1997 profits upwards to 315 billion drachmas, following the acceptance of Norwegian firm Telenor's offer for a 30 percent share of Cosmote, the mobile phone system.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday revealed a plan for peaceful intervention on a political and economic levels which will encourage democracy, stability and economic growth in the Balkans. The plans will be discussed at a Balkan foreign ministers' meeting tentatively scheduled for June 9-10 in Thessaloniki.

--Statistics have revealed a boom in the construction sector, with licences for new buildings up 20.7 percent. The increase in building activity is being attributed to lower interest rates for housing loans.

--Greek and foreign shipowners will now have the ability to invest in new ships or ship repairs with low-interest subsidised loans, according to a new omnibus bill designed to increase incentives for Greek shipbuilding and repair.

--Further cutbacks in public spending are back on the government's agenda following news that state inflows are not at levels forecast. Experts say lost ground cannot be made up and must be dealt with by the more effective management and handing of the public debt as well as distribution of state spending.
--The Bank of Greece closed the previous fiscal year with net profits of 36.6 billion drachmas, up from 34.9 in 1995. Dividends will come to 1,300 drachmas.

--The G. Apostolopoulos Group is to establish five new diagnostic centres in Balkan capitals, in cooperation with the Henri Dunant Institute of the Greek Red Cross and the Euromerchant Balkan Fund, belonging to the Latsis Group.
--Property belonging to Cretabank - the previous Bank of Crete - will be transferred to the new bank without any financial obligations, before its sale.
--The Mortgage Bank made profits of 36 billion drachmas last fiscal year, 10-15 percent up on the previous year, according to sources.
--The Bank of Greece's lending to the state fell by 2.9 percent - or 40 billion drachmas - last year, according to the bank's latest report. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
